scope: Source runtime through real mutually authenticated TLS and SSH gateways on an isolated local Docker Desktop Linux/arm64 network. Not a personal VM, production network listener, direct dockerd TLS configuration or native/frozen app acceptance.
implementation: Existing framework named-context snapshots, credential copying, sandbox lifetime and acknowledged recovery are reused unchanged. No product runtime fix was required.
The thin example consumer uses a byte-forwarding mutual-TLS gateway to the existing filtered Unix socket and shares the actual execution/disconnect consumer with SSH.
The host acceptance shares its real-daemon isolation and lifecycle harness between SSH and TLS. No fake HTTP/daemon responses or external account calls.
verified: Real Docker named-context execution retains trusted CA and client credentials in the existing private per-operation context snapshot. A healthy sandbox program completes through the TLS gateway.

The actual client rejects untrusted server CA and wrong server hostname. The server rejects missing and untrusted client certificates before forwarding HTTP. The harness requires exact PEER_DID_NOT_RETURN_A_CERTIFICATE and CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED server reasons.

After an acknowledged running analysis starts, killing the gateway interrupts its real transport. Owner-stdin EOF stops the analysis before reconnection or explicit removal, in both TLS and SSH cases.
Unreachable cleanup returns unconfirmed with one pending acknowledged receipt. Reconnecting to the same gateway identity and explicitly recovering confirms absence and retires the receipt.
Per transport, proxy logs show exactly two creates and two starts: one completed and one interrupted analysis. Cleanup creates no run/artifact and never replays generated code.

Controller and gateway run uid/gid 1001 with read-only roots, no capabilities and bounded resources. The controller receives neither Docker socket nor private ledger; gateway receives only the filtered socket.
All fixture containers, private/key/data/socket volumes and internal networks are removed. The unrelated llm-cli-proxy service remains running.

fixture.network: Disposable internal bridge; proxy network none. TLS/SSH ports never published to host.
fixture.tls: Python/OpenSSL TLS server requires client certificates and TLS 1.2 minimum; Docker Go client verifies CA and server SAN. No verification bypass flags.
fixture.certificates: Fresh one-day RSA2048 client/server certificates and an untrusted authority. Separate 0700 runtime volumes with 0600 files. CA private keys exist only in initializer tmpfs. No personal credentials are read.
fixture.authority: Only the trusted filtering proxy receives the real daemon socket and private ownership ledger. That authority remains root-equivalent as documented. Gateways receive only its filtered Unix socket.

fixture_preparation: Early probes correctly rejected missing clients but expected a specific Docker diagnostic. TLS 1.3 surfaced EOF/reset instead. The completed harness requires precise server-side SSL rejection reasons; no product failure was inferred from that fixture assertion.

compatibility.upgrade: Acceptance-only additions. Existing deployments need no migration, runtime setting change, application build or DMG rebuild. Build only the explicit test fixture to repeat this gate.
compatibility.rollback: Remove the optional test recipe/consumer/harness extensions; existing execution and records are unchanged.
compatibility.historical_evidence: The original SSH checkpoint retains its historical source/image hashes. This checkpoint verifies the updated shared consumer and both current transport paths.

pending: Personal HTTPS VM install/TLS/auth, real bind paths and mapped ownership, SSH access, upgrades and full restore.
Actual Docker daemon restart, host power-loss and network partitions beyond terminating a disposable gateway.
Production dockerd TLS provisioning, certificate expiry/rotation/revocation and changed SSH aliases/DNS/credentials/host keys.
Physical devices, selected service accounts, escaped MCP descendants and frozen/installed native Windows/Linux/macOS checks.

quality.ruff: All four changed/new Python consumer and test modules pass without exclusions.

certificate_lifecycle_followup.scope: Actual local certificate expiry, same-CA renewal and overlapping/withdrawn CA trust. Historical TLS/disconnection evidence is unchanged; per-leaf revocation and production provisioning remain separate.
